_why_b6c70282: THE GUARD DENIED EVERY TOOL CALL IN A CORRECTLY-LAUNCHED SEAT, and did it silently. 18108039's SessionStart announced a verified anchor by appending `export TF_CLAUDE_GUARD_ANCHOR_OK=1` to the file at CLAUDE_ENV_FILE; PreToolUse and TaskCompleted read that name from their OWN process env. Nothing carried it across. MEASURED 2026-08-16 in the shipped claude.exe: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE is placed in the hook child's environment for SessionStart/Setup/CwdChanged/FileChanged ONLY, and its documented purpose is to apply env to subsequent BASH TOOL commands — it is never turned into a later hook subprocess's environment. Fail-CLOSED, which is exactly why three seats could not see it: a refused seat and a well-behaved seat produce identical receipts. The old suite covered both ENDS of that handshake — the producer by reading the env file, the consumer by being handed a fabricated env — and never the wire. TWO GREEN HALF-HANDSHAKES ARE NOT A HANDSHAKE. b6c70282 DELETES that variable rather than rerouting it (a marker that propagates while naming no session, worktree, branch, commit or pin is the FAIL-OPEN version of the same bug) and replaces it with a marker in the worktree's own git directory, BOUND to session_id + worktree + git_dir + branch + head + this pin + this bundle, with worktree, git dir, branch and head RE-MEASURED from the live tree on every tool call. Cleanliness stays a START condition — a working seat dirties its own tree — and HEAD is advance-only via `merge-base --is-ancestor`, so the seat can still commit. The marker is itself SELF_PROTECTED, with a Bash fence token. 44 files now, not 42: guard-session-marker.mjs and claude-hook-lifecycle.test.mjs are new, and claude_toolbox.mjs derives the file set from `git ls-tree`, so no list needed editing.

session_anchor._expected_head_is_a_ref_on_purpose: resume-anchor-guard resolves expected_head with `rev-parse <x>^{commit}`, so a REF NAME works and a pinned SHA would go stale on the next commit — a guard that is stale by design gets disabled by whoever it annoys. Anchoring to the branch still catches a detached HEAD, the wrong branch, and a checkout that is not at the branch tip.
session_anchor._dirty_disposition: AR-1265 §4 REPLACES the standing block. The desk refused BOTH remedies the worker could have taken alone: do NOT commit the timestamp-only docs/wave25-exit-engine-ab-report.md merely to make the guard green, and do NOT set require_clean:false. Instead this exception pins the exact path AND the sha256 of the exact `git diff HEAD --binary -- <path>` bytes. Any future edit to that file changes the diff and blocks SessionStart, so the historical finding is preserved without letting anything else hide behind the same filename. diff_sha256 was COMPUTED and cross-checked by two instruments (the guard's own dirtyDiffSha256 and `git diff | sha256sum`), never hand-copied.
session_anchor._still_forbidden: A blanket allow-dirty, a glob, a directory, an entry with no diff hash, an entry with no authority, and allowed_dirty combined with require_clean:false are all refused by resume-anchor-guard by construction, not by convention. Untracked files remain blocking and cannot be laundered by listing them.

edit_scope._not_listed_is_not_allowed: Runtime, PAPER, broker/Topstep, compiler execution semantics and the backtester are absent deliberately. AR-1249 §12 and AR-1254 §12 keep them LOCKED, and Worker-2 production authority is not unlocked here.
edit_scope._claude_prefix_is_not_authority_over_the: `.claude/` appears above, but AR-1263 §7A self-protection is evaluated FIRST and is never scope-overridable — this manifest, .claude/settings*.json, .claude/hooks/ and the pinned toolbox all DENY regardless of what this list says. That is deliberate: a worker must never gain permission to edit the file that declares its own permissions merely because a broad prefix covers it.

g2_precall._why_a_native_call_manifest: AR-1267 §6.2. The queue's task_input_sha256 binds the LOGICAL task; it says nothing about the bytes that reach the model, so a permit for the right condition could accompany a prompt carrying a batch answer, a prior winner or a GPT hint. This artifact was frozen BEFORE any answer exists, derived only from the frozen queue, the frozen benchmark packet and the pinned transcript, and the pre-call guard hash-matches the ACTUAL Agent tool input against it. It is an EXECUTION-layer artifact: it does not select, reorder, add to or remove from the eight-condition queue.
g2_precall._why_enabled_now: AR-1265 §5.4. With PreToolUse now registering Agent/Task, a G2-shaped subagent dispatch without a valid durable pre-call permit is refused BEFORE the model call. Post-call refusal cannot un-spend a one-shot attempt. enabled stays true here: isG2Shaped() content-detection (queue path / receipt dir / condition-ref references, g2-precall-guard.mjs:261-278) remains fail-closed for any call that actually touches G2-D surface, independent of strict_session.
g2_precall._why_strict_session_was_true_2026-08-17_: AR-1299A §4 authorized cpb-2026-08-17-0004 for packet AR-1278, the dedicated G2 execution packet, and strict_session=true reclassified EVERY Agent/Task dispatch as G2-shaped for the duration of that dedicated session (g2-precall-guard.mjs:536-538: 'strict session => EVERY subagent dispatch needs a valid permit, full stop'), armed by the Phase 1 control-plane seat as the final configuration step before that session began.
g2_precall._why_strict_session_is_false_now: Operator-authorized 2026-08-19. AR-1278/G2-D is CLOSED — AR-1327A §10 'CLOSED / DO-NOT-REOPEN LIST' explicitly lists 'G2 model calls', and AR-1340A independently forbids replaying the historical G2D correction round per video. The strict blanket therefore had no live authorized session to apply to and was blocking the unrelated, newly-authorized AR-1340A Stage-1/Stage-2 factory-pilot dispatch (worker-1 AR-1341, docs/replay-results/worker-advisor-reports/AR-1341-WORKER1-AR1340A-G2-PRECALL-GUARD-BLOCKS-DISPATCH-2026-08-19.md, Option A). Applied from outside the guarded session per the manifest's own self-protection design (a reviewed commit, not a self-widened scope) — mirrors the symmetric act the previous note already named ('Flipping this to true is a deliberate act for the execution session, not a default'; flipping it back off is the same act in reverse once that session closed). This does NOT weaken G2-D protection: isG2Shaped() content-based detection stays armed and will still deny any call that references the frozen queue/receipt dir/condition refs without a valid permit — only the blanket strict-session override is removed. If a future G2-D session needs strict mode again, that is a new deliberate arm, not a default to inherit from this entry.

finish._why_disabled: claude-finish-check needs a committed receipt file describing a finished packet. G2-D has not run, so there is no finished packet to check and enabling it would make TaskCompleted assert against a receipt that does not exist. It is switched on when a real finish receipt exists — an enabled check with nothing to check is the false-green shape this desk keeps convicting. AR-1265 §5.7 also holds full `P1 NATIVE ACTIVE` back until TaskCompleted finish enforcement is proven, and AR-1264 §7 reported that claude-finish-check still carries the old structural REVIEW_REQUIRED problem — it will bite the moment finish is armed.
